EXTRA CLASS · MANNERS · 32 CARDS · AGES 3–5

Manners flashcards — 32 good habits to print and practise.

Thirty-two printable manners cards for ages three to five: the magic words, the waiting, the tidying, the table manners and the kind hands. Every card below prints free, downloads as a full-size image and carries one plain tip from the teacher on how to practise it tonight — the whole class lives on this single page.

More extra classes ↗
HOW THIS CLASS WORKS

Print the card. Practise the manner. Catch them doing it.

Pick one card a week and pin it to the fridge at your child’s eye level. Name the manner at a calm moment — not mid-tantrum — act it out once together, then spend the week catching the real thing: “You waited your turn — that’s the card!” Children repeat what gets noticed, and a fridge card gets noticed every single day.

The cards run in file order from ask-first to wipe-the-table, but any order works: start with the manner your mornings need most. Print on A4 or Letter paper, cut along the border, and let your child pin up each card they earn — ownership is half of manners. Everything on this page is free to print at home, today.

THE CARDS · 32 MANNERS

Every manner, its tip, and the button to print it.

Each tile is the card itself: the artwork prints at full size with the Download button, and Print runs just that one card through your printer. The tip under each card is the whole lesson — one way to set it up tonight.

AROUND THE SCHOOL

Where manners are practised next.

Practise good manners in Class 32 · Ages 4–5 ↗Kind actions in Class 38 · Ages 4–5 ↗Table manners in the Cafeteria · Ages 2–5 ↗Fair play in the Playground · The five manners ↗The parents’ shelf in the library · All 32 cards ↗All the extra classes ↗

Class 32 builds the daily habits and Class 38 grows the kind words; the Cafeteria room names every food on the tray, and the Playground keeps the five manners that make play fair. This page is the lesson — it teaches each manner to your child the way a teacher would. Parents who want the whole deck on one wall will find it on the parents’ shelf in the flashcards library: the same thirty-two cards, downloading and printing straight from there.

Manners are not a lecture. They are fifty small chances a day for a child to be proudly capable — the cards just help everyone remember to look for the chances.
